summary.tradeoffs: No explicit autoSave in the hook — resumeToolExecution uses *Model receiver so direct reassignment doesn't work. The skill state mutates m in place and persists through the normal save flow.
summary.done: Added post-execution hook for skill_load in stream.go resumeToolExecution loop. On success, sets Session.Skill.Current to the loaded skill name and clears Next. Placed right after set_working_dir block.
summary.decisions: Set Current (not Next) since skill_load already loaded the skill. Cleared Next to avoid stale pending state.
summary.lessons_learned: resumeToolExecution has *Model receiver, so m, _ = m.autoSave() fails type mismatch. Had to drop the autoSave call and rely on in-place mutation.

4.1.name: Inject synthetic skill-load message on send

summary.decisions: Placed injectSkillChangeSynthetic and getSkillText in skill_cycle.go alongside cycleSkill for cohesion. getSkillText loads skill body from registry for rich context.
summary.done: Added skill change check at the start of sendMessage(). If Next != Current, injects a synthetic message with appropriate text (new skill loaded / skill changed / skill unloaded), then liquidates Next into Current. Added injectSkillChangeSynthetic and getSkillText helpers in skill_cycle.go.
summary.tradeoffs: sendMessage takes value receiver so helper calls use (&m) pointer. The synthetic message gets appended before the user message so the model sees the skill context.

5.1.name: Clear Skill on new session / incognito

summary.done: No code changes needed. Both clearSession and toggleIncognito call chatSession.clear() which replaces Session with NewSessionFile(). Since SessionSkill is a value type, the new Session has Skill: {"": ""} — already zeroed. Verified that NewSessionFile does not set Skill field, relying on Go zero values.
summary.lessons_learned: NewSessionFile doesn't explicitly set every field, Go zero values fill in the rest. SessionSkill{} is the correct default.
summary.decisions: No code change — existing clear path already handles it correctly via zero-value semantics.
